questions.q: How many players does one soccer team have on the field, including the goalkeeper?
questions.x: Each side fields ten outfield players and one goalkeeper. A team must keep at least seven players on the field to continue a match.

questions.q: Which city hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics?
questions.x: The opening ceremony took place at the Bird's Nest stadium on 08/08/08 at 8:08 pm, a date chosen because 8 is a lucky number in China.

questions.q: On which surface is the Wimbledon tennis tournament played?
questions.x: Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam still played on natural grass. Players are also required to wear almost entirely white clothing.

questions.q: How many interlocking rings appear on the Olympic flag?
questions.x: The five rings represent the five inhabited continents joined together. The flag was introduced in 1914 and first flown at the 1920 Games.

questions.q: Which country won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
questions.x: Uruguay hosted and won the first tournament, beating neighbors Argentina 4-2 in the final in Montevideo.

questions.q: In golf, what is a score of one stroke under par on a hole called?
questions.x: The term 'birdie' comes from early American slang, where 'bird' meant something excellent. It was coined around 1899 in Atlantic City.

questions.q: Michael Jordan won six NBA championships with which team?
questions.x: The Bulls won two separate runs of three straight titles, in 1991-93 and 1996-98. Jordan was Finals MVP every time.

questions.q: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football?
questions.x: A touchdown is worth six points, and the team can then try for one or two extra points. Before 1912 a touchdown was worth only five points.

questions.q: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
questions.x: Athens was chosen to honor the ancient Games' Greek origins. About 240 athletes from 14 nations took part.

questions.q: How many holes are played in a standard full round of golf?
questions.x: The standard of 18 holes was set at St Andrews in Scotland in 1764, when the club reduced its course from 22 holes to 18.

questions.q: Which sport is played with a shuttlecock?
questions.x: Badminton is named after Badminton House in England, where the game became popular in the 1870s. Its feathered shuttlecock traditionally has 16 feathers.

questions.q: What color card does a referee show to send a soccer player off the field?
questions.x: Cards were introduced at the 1970 World Cup after English referee Ken Aston got the idea while stopped at a traffic light.

questions.q: How many players from each team are on the court at once in basketball?
questions.x: Each team can use more than five players in a game through substitutions, but only five may be on the court at a time.

questions.q: Sumo wrestling is the traditional national sport of which country?
questions.x: Sumo has been practiced in Japan for well over a thousand years and has Shinto religious roots. Bouts are often over in a few seconds.

questions.q: What is the official distance of a marathon?
questions.x: The exact distance is 26 miles 385 yards, or 42.195 kilometers. It was standardized after the 1908 London Olympics.

questions.q: How many bases are there on a baseball diamond, counting home plate?
questions.x: Runners must touch first, second and third base in order before reaching home plate to score. The bases are 90 feet apart.

questions.q: What was the birth name of the boxer Muhammad Ali?
questions.x: He won Olympic light heavyweight gold in 1960 as Cassius Clay. He changed his name in 1964 after joining the Nation of Islam.

questions.q: The Tour de France is a famous race in which sport?
questions.x: The first Tour de France was held in 1903. The race lasts about three weeks and covers more than 3,000 kilometers.

questions.q: Sprinter Usain Bolt represents which country?
questions.x: Bolt won the 100 m and 200 m at both the 2008 and 2012 Olympics. He grew up in Trelawny, Jamaica, and first loved cricket.

questions.q: In which sport do two packs of forwards push against each other in a scrum?
questions.x: The scrum is a way of restarting play after a minor rule break. In rugby union each pack has eight forwards.

questions.q: Which Olympic sport features events on the pommel horse and rings?
questions.x: These are two of the six apparatuses in men's artistic gymnastics. Gymnastics has been part of every modern Olympic Games since 1896.

questions.q: How many players are in a cricket team on the field?
questions.x: Each side fields eleven players, including the wicketkeeper. Only two batters from the batting team are on the field at a time.

questions.q: Which country hosted the 2014 FIFA World Cup?
questions.x: It was Brazil's second time hosting the men's tournament, after 1950. Germany beat Argentina 1-0 in the final at the Maracana.

questions.q: Which city hosted the 2012 Summer Olympics?
questions.x: London became the first city to host the modern Summer Games three times, after 1908 and 1948.

questions.q: In which sport do teams compete in the Super Bowl?

questions.q: Which Olympic medal is awarded for second place?

questions.q: Which team sport awards the Stanley Cup?

questions.q: In which country did the sport of cricket originate?

questions.q: Tennis star Roger Federer comes from which country?

questions.q: Against which team did Diego Maradona score his 'Hand of God' goal in 1986?

questions.q: How long is a standard professional soccer match, not counting stoppage time?
questions.x: A match is two halves of 45 minutes each, with a short break at halftime. Referees add stoppage time for delays.

questions.q: How many players per team are on the court in a volleyball match?
questions.x: Teams rotate positions each time they win the serve. Volleyball was invented in 1895 in Massachusetts.

questions.q: In tennis scoring, what does the term 'love' mean?

questions.q: What is the maximum score in a single game of ten-pin bowling?
questions.x: A perfect game requires twelve consecutive strikes. Each frame can score up to 30 when strikes follow strikes.

questions.q: What shape is a standard boxing ring?
questions.x: Despite the name 'ring', the ring is square, with ropes on four sides. The name comes from the earlier circles drawn by spectators.

questions.q: Which swimming stroke is most commonly used in freestyle events?

questions.q: In which sport might you see a triple axel?

questions.q: What does the Olympic motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' mean?

questions.q: In which Greek location is the Olympic flame lit before each Games?

questions.q: The 'All Blacks' is the nickname of which country's national rugby union team?
questions.x: The team is famous for performing the haka before matches. They wear an all-black uniform with a silver fern emblem.

questions.q: The Masters golf tournament is held each year at which course?
questions.x: The winner is awarded a green jacket. The course is in Augusta, Georgia, and is famed for its azaleas.

questions.q: Which small principality hosts a famous Formula One street race through its city?

questions.q: Lionel Messi was born in which country?
questions.x: Messi was born in Rosario, Argentina, and moved to Barcelona at age 13. He won the Ballon d'Or several times before 2015.

questions.q: How many Grand Slam tennis tournaments are played each year?
questions.x: They are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open. Winning all four in one calendar year is called a Grand Slam.

questions.q: What is it called when a soccer player scores three goals in one match?

questions.q: In golf, what is it called when a player sinks the ball in one stroke from the tee?
questions.x: The odds of an ordinary golfer making a hole-in-one on a given par-3 are around 12,000 to one.

questions.q: In which sport do England and Australia compete for the Ashes?

questions.q: In which sport is a home run scored?
questions.x: A home run usually happens when the batter hits the ball over the outfield fence in fair territory, allowing everyone to circle the bases.

questions.q: Which Spanish city hosted the 1992 Summer Olympics?
questions.x: The 1992 Games were the first with NBA players in the US basketball team, known as the Dream Team.

questions.q: Which Australian city hosted the 2000 Summer Olympics?
questions.x: Australia has hosted the Summer Games twice, in Melbourne in 1956 and in Sydney in 2000.

questions.q: Which US city hosted the 1996 Summer Olympics?
questions.x: The 1996 Games marked the 100th anniversary of the modern Olympics. Muhammad Ali lit the Olympic cauldron.

questions.q: Which South Korean city hosted the 1988 Summer Olympics?
questions.x: The Seoul Games included table tennis and tennis as full medal sports, the latter returning after a 64-year break.

questions.q: Which Japanese city hosted the 1998 Winter Olympics?
questions.x: Nagano was the second Japanese city to host the Winter Games, after Sapporo in 1972.

questions.q: Which Canadian city hosted the 2010 Winter Olympics?
questions.x: Vancouver's Games were held in February 2010. Calgary had earlier hosted the 1988 Winter Olympics.

questions.q: Which two countries co-hosted the 2002 FIFA World Cup?

questions.q: Which African country hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup?

questions.q: Which country won the 2006 FIFA World Cup in Germany?

questions.q: Which country won the 2010 FIFA World Cup?

questions.q: Which country won the 1966 FIFA World Cup on home soil?

questions.q: How many strikes make an out for a batter in baseball?
questions.x: The same batter also walks to first base after four balls. 'Three strikes and you're out' became a common saying in everyday English.

questions.q: How high above the floor is a regulation basketball hoop?

questions.q: How many players are in a rugby union team on the field?

questions.q: How many players per team, including the goalie, are on the ice in a standard ice hockey game?

questions.q: How many gold medals did swimmer Michael Phelps win at the 2008 Beijing Olympics?

questions.q: Which gymnast scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic history, in 1976?

questions.q: What color jersey does the Tour de France race leader wear?

questions.q: Who invented basketball in 1891?

questions.q: The Kentucky Derby is a famous event in which sport?

questions.q: In which sport do teams slide granite stones toward a target called the house?

questions.q: Taekwondo, a martial art and Olympic sport, originated in which country?

questions.q: How often is the men's FIFA World Cup normally held?

questions.q: Which country had won the men's soccer World Cup five times by 2014?

questions.q: What color is a standard tennis ball in major professional tournaments?

questions.q: In baseball, what is the name of the player who throws the ball to the batter?

questions.q: In which country is the Wimbledon tennis tournament played?

questions.q: Which surface is used for the French Open tennis tournament?

questions.q: Babe Ruth is a legend of which sport?

questions.q: Which city hosted the 1984 Summer Olympics?

questions.q: In which country do clubs like Manchester United and Arsenal play?

questions.q: How many points is a free throw worth in basketball?

questions.q: How many points is a try worth in rugby union?

questions.q: Which swimming stroke is named after an insect?

questions.q: In soccer, what is the name of the box-shaped area in front of each goal where a keeper can use their hands?

questions.q: Which country won the 1998 FIFA World Cup on home soil?

questions.q: In which Australian city is the Australian Open tennis tournament held?

questions.q: In which sport do competitors race around gates in a slalom event?

questions.q: How many players does a baseball team have on the field when playing defense?

questions.q: What is the name for a score of two strokes under par on a golf hole?

questions.q: Which weight division is the heaviest in professional boxing's traditional classes?

questions.q: How many periods are played in a standard ice hockey game?

questions.q: Which track and field event involves throwing a heavy metal ball?

questions.q: Brazil's national soccer team is famous for wearing which color shirt?

questions.q: Which Olympic event combines swimming, cycling and running?

questions.q: In which sport are the terms 'deuce' and 'advantage' used?

questions.q: How far is the penalty spot from the goal line in soccer?

questions.q: Which team did France beat 3-0 in the 1998 World Cup final?

questions.q: Which Swedish tennis player won five consecutive Wimbledon titles from 1976 to 1980?

questions.q: Which golf major is traditionally awarded with the Claret Jug?

questions.q: What is the diameter of a standard basketball hoop's rim?

questions.q: What is the trophy of the Rugby World Cup called?

questions.q: What is a batter's score of 100 runs called in cricket?

questions.q: Which country won the first Rugby World Cup, in 1987?

questions.q: Which British runner was the first to break the four-minute mile, in 1954?

questions.q: Which German tennis player won the 1988 calendar-year Grand Slam and an Olympic gold?

questions.q: Which Australian tennis legend won the calendar-year Grand Slam in both 1962 and 1969?

questions.q: How long is the pitch between the wickets in cricket?

questions.q: How many players per team are on the field in Australian rules football?
questions.x: Each team also has four substitutes on the interchange bench. The oval field can be up to 185 meters long.

questions.q: Which basketball team did Bill Russell win 11 NBA championships with?

questions.q: Which New York Yankees first baseman was nicknamed 'the Iron Horse'?

questions.q: In 1947, Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball's color barrier with which team?

questions.q: Ayrton Senna, a three-time Formula One champion, was from which country?

questions.q: Which German driver won five consecutive Formula One titles from 2000 to 2004?
questions.x: Schumacher won those titles driving for Ferrari, ending a long title drought for the Italian team that had lasted since 1979.

questions.q: The Daytona 500 stock car race is held in which US state?
questions.x: Held at Daytona International Speedway each February, the race is the opening event of the NASCAR season.

questions.q: Which Italian car maker uses a prancing horse as its racing emblem?

questions.q: The 24 Hours of Le Mans endurance race takes place in which country?

questions.q: In golf, what is the name for a score of three strokes under par on one hole?

questions.q: Which golfer was nicknamed 'the Golden Bear'?

questions.q: Which Australian golfer was nicknamed 'the Great White Shark'?

questions.q: Which team won the first Cricket World Cup in 1975?

questions.q: Which country won the 1983 Cricket World Cup, beating the West Indies in the final?

questions.q: Which Australian batsman finished his Test career with an average of 99.94?
questions.x: Bradman needed just four runs in his final innings to average 100 but was bowled for a duck.

questions.q: Which city hosted the 1900 Olympics, the first Games in which women competed?

questions.q: Who founded the International Olympic Committee in 1894 and revived the modern Games?

questions.q: How many players per team are in the water in a water polo match, including the goalkeeper?

questions.q: How many points is a drop goal worth in rugby union?

questions.q: What is the name of the traditional Maori war dance performed by the New Zealand national rugby team?

questions.q: Which American won the first women's Olympic marathon, at the 1984 Los Angeles Games?

questions.q: Which Finnish distance runner, nicknamed the 'Flying Finn', won nine Olympic gold medals?

questions.q: Which fruit is traditionally served with cream at the Wimbledon Championships?

questions.q: What is the maximum number of sets in a men's Grand Slam singles match?

questions.q: Which Parisian stadium hosts the French Open?

questions.q: Which 17-year-old German won Wimbledon in 1985?

questions.q: Which national team, led by Johan Cruyff, popularized 'Total Football' in the 1970s?

questions.q: Which English captain lifted the World Cup trophy in 1966?

questions.q: Who scored a hat-trick for England in the 1966 World Cup final?

questions.q: Which Spanish club plays its home matches at Camp Nou?

questions.q: Which English club plays its home matches at Old Trafford?

questions.q: Biathlon combines cross-country skiing with which other discipline?

questions.q: What type of rock are curling stones traditionally made from?

questions.q: How many players make up a curling team?

questions.q: How long is a minor penalty in ice hockey?

questions.q: How many major championships are there in men's professional golf?

questions.q: What is the maximum number of clubs a golfer may carry during a round?

questions.q: Which trophy is awarded to the winner of the Super Bowl?

questions.q: How many innings are in a standard Major League Baseball game?

questions.q: What is it called when a baseball batter receives four balls and advances to first base?

questions.q: In which US city is Fenway Park, one of baseball's oldest stadiums?
questions.x: Fenway Park opened in 1912 and is the home of the Red Sox. Its tall left-field wall is known as the Green Monster.

questions.q: In which US city is Wrigley Field, home of the Cubs?
questions.x: Wrigley Field opened in 1914 and is famous for its ivy-covered outfield walls. It did not have lights for night games until 1988.

questions.q: How many seconds is the shot clock in NBA basketball?
questions.x: The 24-second clock was introduced in 1954 to speed up the game, which had become slow and low scoring.

questions.q: What is the name of Major League Baseball's annual championship series?
questions.x: Despite the name, only teams from the United States and Canada take part. The first modern series was in 1903. It is also nicknamed the Fall Classic.

questions.q: Which of cycling's Grand Tours takes place in Italy?
questions.x: The Giro leader wears a pink jersey, because the sponsoring newspaper, La Gazzetta dello Sport, is printed on pink paper.

questions.q: What does the polka-dot jersey signify in the Tour de France?
questions.x: The jersey is white with red dots. It is awarded to the rider who earns the most points on the major mountain climbs.

questions.q: On which river does the annual Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race take place?
questions.x: The race has been held since 1829 on a 4.2-mile stretch in London between Putney and Mortlake.

questions.q: Which fencing weapon, along with foil and sabre, is used in Olympic competition?
questions.x: Fencing has been in every modern Olympics. In epee, a touch can be scored anywhere on the body.

questions.q: What is the highest rank in professional sumo wrestling?
questions.x: A yokozuna cannot be demoted and is expected to retire if they can no longer perform. They wear a special white rope belt.

questions.q: In which African country did Muhammad Ali fight George Foreman in the 1974 'Rumble in the Jungle'?
questions.x: The fight took place in Kinshasa, now in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Ali used his 'rope-a-dope' tactic to win by knockout.

questions.q: Which American heavyweight boxer was nicknamed the 'Brown Bomber'?
questions.x: Louis held the heavyweight title for nearly 12 years, from 1937 to 1949, defending it a record 25 times.

questions.q: Which Soviet gymnast charmed audiences at the 1972 Olympics and popularized a backward somersault on the beam?
questions.x: Korbut won three gold medals in 1972. Her fame helped spark a boom in gymnastics around the world.

questions.q: How many events make up the women's heptathlon?
questions.x: The events are spread over two days. The men's equivalent, the decathlon, has ten events.

questions.q: Which Australian runner lit the Olympic cauldron at the 2000 Sydney Games?
questions.x: Freeman went on to win the 400 m gold in front of a home crowd, after emerging from a pool of water in the ceremony.

questions.q: Which North London club is nicknamed 'the Gunners'?
questions.x: The club was founded in 1886 by workers at the Royal Arsenal armaments factory in Woolwich.

questions.q: Pele spent most of his club career at which Brazilian club?
questions.x: Pele joined Santos at age 15 and stayed for almost two decades. He also played in the United States for the New York Cosmos.

questions.q: What was the original name of the UEFA Champions League when it began in 1955?
questions.x: The tournament was proposed by the French sports newspaper L'Equipe. Real Madrid won the first five editions.

questions.q: At which Olympics did the American 'Dream Team' of NBA stars first compete?
questions.x: Before 1992, only amateurs were allowed to play for the US team. The Dream Team won gold by an average of more than 40 points.

questions.q: In cricket, what does LBW stand for?
questions.x: A batter can be out LBW if the ball would have hit the stumps but was blocked by the batter's leg or body.

questions.q: How many legal deliveries are in a standard over in cricket?
questions.x: In the past some countries used eight-ball overs, including Australia until the 1979-80 season.

questions.q: Which country joined the Five Nations rugby tournament in 2000 to make it the Six Nations?
questions.x: Italy beat Scotland 34-20 in its debut match. The tournament had previously included England, Scotland, Ireland, Wales and France.

questions.q: Which fly-half kicked England's winning drop goal in the 2003 Rugby World Cup final?
questions.x: The kick came in the final seconds of extra time against Australia in Sydney, giving England a 20-17 victory.

questions.q: Which country won the 1995 Rugby World Cup on home soil?
questions.x: South Africa beat New Zealand 15-12 in extra time. Nelson Mandela famously presented the trophy wearing a Springbok jersey.

questions.q: What is the maximum break in a frame of snooker?
questions.x: It requires potting all 15 reds with 15 blacks, then all six colors in order. It is known as a maximum break.

questions.q: What is the highest score possible with three darts in one turn?
questions.x: It is achieved with three treble 20s. Many pub players dream of hitting it, and crowds traditionally cheer a loud 'one hundred and eighty!'

questions.q: In which sport did Eddie 'the Eagle' Edwards become a cult hero at the 1988 Winter Olympics?
questions.x: Michael 'Eddie' Edwards from England was the only British ski jumper at the Calgary Games and finished last in both events.

questions.q: Which music did British ice dancers Torvill and Dean skate to for their 1984 Olympic gold?
questions.x: Their Sarajevo routine to Ravel's Bolero earned a perfect set of nine 6.0 marks for artistic impression.

questions.q: Which team did the United States beat in the 1980 'Miracle on Ice' hockey game?
questions.x: A team of American college players upset the favored Soviets 4-3 at Lake Placid. They then beat Finland to win gold.

questions.q: Which basketball player scored 100 points in a single NBA game in 1962?
questions.x: Chamberlain's Philadelphia Warriors beat the New York Knicks 169-147 in Hershey, Pennsylvania. The game was not televised.

questions.q: Which NBA team plays its home games at Madison Square Garden?
questions.x: The current Garden is the fourth building to use the name. It also hosts boxing, concerts and ice hockey.

questions.q: Which jersey number did hockey star Wayne Gretzky wear, later retired across the NHL?
questions.x: Gretzky's number 99 was retired by the whole league in 2000. He was nicknamed 'The Great One'.

questions.q: The Cy Young Award honors excellence in which baseball role?
questions.x: It is named after Cy Young, who won 511 games as a pitcher, a total that is unlikely ever to be beaten.

questions.q: How many yards must an American football offense gain to earn a first down?
questions.x: The offense has four chances, called downs, to advance 10 yards. If it fails, the ball goes to the other team.

questions.q: How long is an American football field between the two goal lines?
questions.x: The end zones add 10 yards at each end, so the whole field is 120 yards. The field is 53 and a third yards wide.

questions.q: Which Olympic champion swimmer later starred as Tarzan in Hollywood films?
questions.x: Weissmuller won five Olympic golds in the 1920s and later made 12 Tarzan films.

questions.q: Which Asian city hosted the 1964 Summer Olympics, the first Games held in Asia?
questions.x: The Tokyo Games were the first broadcast internationally by satellite. Judo made its Olympic debut there.

questions.q: Which Norwegian town hosted the 1994 Winter Olympics?
questions.x: The 1994 Games were held only two years after the 1992 edition, when the schedule was changed so Winter and Summer Games alternate every two years.

questions.q: Which Italian club is nicknamed 'the Old Lady'?
questions.x: Juventus is based in Turin and wears black and white stripes. It has won more Italian league titles than any other club.

questions.q: Which Argentine won five Formula One world titles in the 1950s?
questions.x: Fangio won his titles with four different teams. He was nicknamed 'El Chueco', Spanish for 'the bowlegged one'.

questions.q: Which Parisian avenue is the traditional finish of the Tour de France?
questions.x: The race has finished on the Champs-Elysees since 1975. Before that, it ended at the Parc des Princes or Vel d'Hiv.

questions.q: Which Soviet goalkeeper, nicknamed the 'Black Spider', is a legend of European football?
questions.x: Yashin wore all black and is said to have saved well over 100 penalties. He won the Ballon d'Or in 1963.

questions.q: What does the winner of the Indianapolis 500 traditionally drink in victory lane?
questions.x: The custom began in 1936, when Louis Meyer asked for buttermilk, which his mother had told him refreshes on hot days.

questions.q: Which Summer Olympics, scheduled for Berlin, were cancelled because of World War I?
questions.x: Berlin had been awarded the 1916 Games, but they were never held. The next Games took place in Antwerp in 1920.

questions.q: Which Italian resort hosted the 1956 Winter Olympics?
questions.x: These were the first Winter Games to be televised, with the broadcast reaching several European countries.

questions.q: Which Austrian city hosted the Winter Olympics in both 1964 and 1976?
questions.x: Innsbruck stepped in to host the 1976 Games after Denver withdrew, and so became a two-time host city.

questions.q: Which Ukrainian pole vaulter was the first to clear 6 meters, in 1985?
questions.x: Bubka cleared 6.00 m in Paris in 1985. He went on to break the world record 35 times during his career.

questions.q: Which American sprinter won three gold medals at the 1960 Rome Olympics after overcoming childhood polio?
questions.x: Rudolph won the 100 m, 200 m and 4x100 m relay. Italian crowds nicknamed her 'La Gazzella Nera', the Black Gazelle.

questions.q: Which Belgian cyclist, nicknamed 'The Cannibal', won the Tour de France five times?
questions.x: Merckx won his Tours between 1969 and 1974. In 1969 he took the overall, points and mountains classifications in the same year.

questions.q: On which German circuit did Niki Lauda suffer his near-fatal Formula One crash in 1976?
questions.x: Lauda returned to racing just six weeks later. He went on to win the world title in 1977 and again in 1984.

questions.q: Which English racecourse hosts the Grand National steeplechase?
questions.x: The race has been run over fences at Aintree near Liverpool since 1839. Its fences, such as Becher's Brook, are famous.

questions.q: Who in 1875 became the first person to swim the English Channel without artificial aid?
questions.x: Captain Webb took nearly 22 hours to swim from Dover to Calais. He was said to have used a breaststroke and was greased in porpoise oil.

questions.q: Which Frenchman scored 13 goals at the 1958 World Cup?
questions.x: Fontaine scored his 13 goals in only six matches, and France finished third. Brazil, with 17-year-old Pele, won the title.

questions.q: Which country won the 1992 European Championship in soccer after joining the tournament late as a replacement?
questions.x: Denmark replaced Yugoslavia, which was excluded, just ten days before the tournament and beat Germany 2-0 in the final.

questions.q: In which year was the first Wimbledon Championship played?
questions.x: Only the men's singles was held in 1877, with 22 players. Spencer Gore won the first title.

questions.q: Which team won the first modern World Series in 1903?
questions.x: The Boston Americans, who later became the Red Sox, beat the Pittsburgh Pirates five games to three in a best-of-nine series.

questions.q: Which England captain devised the controversial 'Bodyline' tactics on the 1932-33 tour of Australia?
questions.x: Bodyline involved fast bowlers aiming at the batter's body. It caused such anger that the laws of cricket were later changed.

questions.q: How many consecutive baseball games did Cal Ripken Jr. play between 1982 and 1998?
questions.x: Ripken passed Lou Gehrig's long-standing mark of 2,130 games on September 6, 1995. He was nicknamed 'the Iron Man'.

questions.q: At which Melbourne stadium is the AFL Grand Final traditionally played?
questions.x: The MCG holds more than 90,000 spectators. It also hosted the 1956 Summer Olympics.

questions.q: Which sport is played with a stick called a hurley and a ball called a sliotar?
questions.x: Hurling is an ancient Gaelic game, among the fastest field sports in the world. A sliotar is a leather ball with a raised seam.

questions.q: Which sport was invented in 1895 in Holyoke, Massachusetts, as a gentler alternative to basketball?
questions.x: William G. Morgan originally called it 'mintonette'. A visitor suggested the name volleyball because players 'volley' the ball.

questions.q: What is the highest score that can be checked out with three darts in a single turn?
questions.x: The checkout is two treble 20s followed by a bullseye. A 3-dart finish must end on a double or the bullseye.

questions.q: Which club owns Lord's Cricket Ground and was the long-time guardian of cricket's Laws?
questions.x: The MCC, founded in 1787, wrote the first Laws of Cricket in 1788. Lord's is in north London and is called the 'Home of Cricket'.

questions.q: Which American heavyweight boxer retired undefeated in 1956 with a record of 49 wins and no losses?
questions.x: Marciano knocked out 43 of his opponents. He died in a plane crash in 1969, the day before his 46th birthday.

questions.q: In which country was the 1975 'Thrilla' fight between Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier held?
questions.x: The bout in Manila was the third and final fight between the pair. Frazier's corner stopped the fight before the 15th round.

questions.q: The Paralympic movement grew from games held in 1948 at a hospital in which country?
questions.x: Dr Ludwig Guttmann organized archery for wartime injured at Stoke Mandeville Hospital. The first official Paralympics took place in Rome in 1960.

questions.q: In which event did Bob Beamon leap 8.90 m at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics?
questions.x: Beamon beat the previous world mark by 55 cm, helped by the thin air of Mexico City. It was so far that officials had to measure it by hand with a tape.

questions.q: The marathon distance of 26 miles 385 yards was set at the Olympics in which city?
questions.x: The 1908 course ran from Windsor Castle to the stadium so that the royal family could watch from the start.

questions.q: Which sport is part of modern pentathlon alongside fencing, swimming, shooting and running?
questions.x: The modern pentathlon was devised by Pierre de Coubertin, inspired by the skills of a 19th-century cavalry officer.

questions.q: How much does a men's Olympic hammer weigh?
questions.x: The hammer is a metal ball on a steel wire. It weighs the same as the men's shot put, 16 pounds.

questions.q: Which Rio stadium hosted the 1950 World Cup match in which Uruguay stunned Brazil?
questions.x: Well over 150,000 spectators watched Uruguay win 2-1. The defeat is remembered in Brazil as the 'Maracanazo'.

questions.q: Which Hungarian forward starred for the 'Magical Magyars' and later for Real Madrid?
questions.x: Puskas scored four goals in the 1960 European Cup final for Real Madrid. He was nicknamed 'the Galloping Major'.

questions.q: Which Portuguese star was top scorer at the 1966 World Cup with nine goals?
questions.x: Eusebio scored four goals in a quarter-final comeback against North Korea. He was nicknamed 'the Black Panther'.

questions.q: Who scored two headed goals for France in the 1998 World Cup final?
questions.x: Zidane's goals both came from corner kicks in the first half. France led 2-0 at the interval and Petit added a third.

questions.q: Which trophy did Brazil keep permanently after winning a third World Cup in 1970?
questions.x: The original trophy was later stolen in Brazil in 1983 and never recovered. FIFA introduced a new trophy for 1974.

questions.q: How wide is a standard soccer goal between the posts?
questions.x: That is 7.32 meters. The crossbar stands 8 feet (2.44 m) above the ground.

questions.q: Which Grand Slam tournament was the first to become an open event, in 1968?
questions.x: Open tennis allowed professionals to compete in the major tournaments alongside amateurs. Ken Rosewall won the first men's open title.

questions.q: Which American teenager known as 'Little Mo' won the first women's calendar-year Grand Slam, in 1953?
questions.x: Connolly's career ended at 19 after a horse-riding accident. Her tennis was admired for its accuracy.

questions.q: Who in 1938 became the first man to win all four Grand Slam tennis titles in a single year?
questions.x: The American's feat was unmatched until Rod Laver repeated it in 1962. Budge's backhand was regarded as one of the best of all time.

questions.q: Which former champion lost to Billie Jean King in the 1973 'Battle of the Sexes' tennis match?
questions.x: King won in straight sets in front of about 30,000 fans at the Houston Astrodome and an estimated 90 million TV viewers.

questions.q: The Davis Cup in tennis is named after which American player who donated the trophy?
questions.x: Davis, a Harvard student, designed the competition in 1900 and later became US Secretary of War.

questions.q: Which amateur golfer won the four major tournaments of his era in 1930 and co-founded Augusta National?
questions.x: Jones retired from competition at just 28, after winning the 'Grand Slam' of that time. He was a lawyer by profession.

questions.q: Which Spanish golfer won the Open Championship in 1979, 1984 and 1988?
questions.x: Ballesteros was known for his creative shot-making from trouble. He also won the Masters twice, in 1980 and 1983.

questions.q: Which South African golfer, nicknamed 'The Black Knight', won nine major championships?
questions.x: Player was famous for wearing black on the course and for his fitness. He was one of the first golfers to travel the globe to play.

questions.q: What is the diameter of a golf hole?
questions.x: That is 108 mm. The size was standardized by the Royal and Ancient Golf Club in 1891, based on a piece of drainage pipe used at Musselburgh.

questions.q: Which Scottish course hosted the first Open Championship in 1860?
questions.x: Willie Park Sr. won the first Open, played over three rounds of a 12-hole course, with eight players competing.

questions.q: Which England batsman was bowled by Shane Warne's famous 'Ball of the Century' in 1993?
questions.x: Warne's first ball in Ashes cricket spun sharply from outside leg stump to hit off stump at Old Trafford.

questions.q: Which West Indian all-rounder hit six sixes in one over in a 1968 first-class match?
questions.x: Sobers hit all six off Glamorgan's Malcolm Nash at Swansea, in the first instance in first-class cricket.

questions.q: Which two countries played the first Test match, in 1877?
questions.x: The match was played in Melbourne, and Australia won by 45 runs. Charles Bannerman scored the first Test century.

questions.q: In which Indian city is the Eden Gardens cricket ground?
questions.x: Eden Gardens opened in 1864 and is one of the largest cricket stadiums in the world. It hosted the 1987 and 1996 World Cup semi-finals.

questions.q: The name 'the Ashes' came from a mock obituary of English cricket in which 1882 publication?
questions.x: The notice said English cricket had died and the body would be cremated and the ashes taken to Australia.

questions.q: At which English school, according to legend, did William Webb Ellis first run with the ball in 1823?
questions.x: The legend is widely considered a myth, but it gave the sport its name and the Rugby World Cup its trophy.

questions.q: What were the first basketball goals, nailed to a gym balcony in 1891, made from?
questions.x: Each time a ball went in, someone had to climb up and retrieve it, until the bottoms were cut out of the baskets.

questions.q: In which NBA season was the three-point line first introduced?
questions.x: The ABA had used the three-point shot earlier, in the 1960s. The NBA adopted it after absorbing several ABA teams.

questions.q: Which NBA star was famous for the 'skyhook' shot?
questions.x: Abdul-Jabbar was originally named Lew Alcindor and won six NBA championships. The skyhook was nearly impossible to block.

questions.q: How many games long was Joe DiMaggio's 1941 hitting streak?
questions.x: DiMaggio hit safely in 56 straight games for the Yankees. Many see it as baseball's most unbreakable feat.

questions.q: In which small New York town is the National Baseball Hall of Fame located?
questions.x: A myth claims Abner Doubleday invented baseball in Cooperstown in 1839. The Hall of Fame opened there in 1939.

questions.q: Which Yankees pitcher threw a perfect game in the 1956 World Series?
questions.x: Larsen retired all 27 batters faced in Game 5 against the Brooklyn Dodgers. Yogi Berra famously jumped into his arms.

questions.q: Which team won the first Super Bowl, in January 1967?
questions.x: The Packers beat the Chiefs 35-10 in the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The game was then called the AFL-NFL World Championship.

questions.q: Which NFL team completed a perfect 17-0 season in 1972?
questions.x: The Dolphins went on to win Super Bowl VII. They remain the only NFL team to finish a full season without a loss or tie.

questions.q: The Stanley Cup was donated by Lord Stanley, who held which office in Canada?
questions.x: Lord Stanley of Preston bought the original bowl for about 10 guineas in 1892.

questions.q: Which defenseman scored the famous 'flying' Stanley Cup-winning goal in 1970?
questions.x: Orr's overtime goal for the Boston Bruins against St. Louis was captured in a photo of him airborne after being tripped.

questions.q: Which Norwegian figure skater won Olympic gold in 1928, 1932 and 1936 and became a film star?
questions.x: Henie introduced short skirts and white boots to figure skating. She later starred in Hollywood musicals.

questions.q: Which French skier won all three alpine events at the 1968 Winter Olympics in Grenoble?
questions.x: Killy won the downhill, giant slalom and slalom. The slalom was marred by a dispute after rival Karl Schranz was disqualified.

questions.q: Which Austrian won the dramatic 1976 Olympic downhill, in a run famous for its near-crash?
questions.x: Klammer raced the course on the edge of control and won by just 0.33 seconds before a home crowd.

questions.q: Which US state hosts the Iditarod sled dog race each year?
questions.x: The race of over 1,000 miles commemorates a 1925 serum run to Nome, where dog teams carried medicine to fight a diphtheria outbreak.

questions.q: Which British circuit hosted the first Formula One World Championship race in 1950?
questions.x: King George VI attended the race, which was won by Italian driver Giuseppe Farina in an Alfa Romeo.

questions.q: Which Scottish driver won the Formula One world titles in 1963 and 1965?
questions.x: Clark drove for Lotus and won the Indianapolis 500 in 1965. He died in a Formula Two race in 1968.

questions.q: Which Frenchman nicknamed 'The Professor' won four Formula One world titles?
questions.x: Prost won his titles between 1985 and 1993, and had a famous rivalry with teammate Ayrton Senna.

questions.q: Which British driver won the Monaco Grand Prix, the Indianapolis 500 and the 24 Hours of Le Mans?
questions.x: The trio of races is known as the Triple Crown of Motorsport. Hill won Indy in 1966 and Le Mans in 1972.

questions.q: Which heavyweight boxer was nicknamed 'Smokin' Joe'?
questions.x: Frazier won Olympic gold in 1964 and beat Ali in 1971 in the 'Fight of the Century'. He won on points after 15 rounds.

questions.q: Which British rower won gold at five consecutive Olympics from 1984 to 2000?
questions.x: Redgrave won his fifth gold in Sydney in the coxless four. He had been diagnosed with diabetes in 1997.

questions.q: How many apparatus events are there in men's artistic gymnastics?
questions.x: They are floor, pommel horse, rings, vault, parallel bars and horizontal bar. Women compete on four apparatus.

questions.q: How wide is a gymnastics balance beam?
questions.x: That is only about 4 inches. The beam is 5 meters long and stands 125 cm above the floor.

questions.q: Which Greek runner won the first Olympic marathon in 1896?
questions.x: Louis's win thrilled the home crowd in Athens. He was a water carrier, and his victory was the Games' greatest moment for Greece.

questions.q: In which year BC are the first recorded ancient Olympic Games traditionally dated?
questions.x: The Games were held at Olympia every four years for more than a thousand years, until about AD 393.

questions.q: Which Kenyan runner won the 1500 m at the 1968 Olympics in Mexico City?
questions.x: Keino ran at high altitude and beat favorite Jim Ryun by a huge margin. He later helped inspire generations of Kenyan runners.

questions.q: Which Scottish runner, subject of the film 'Chariots of Fire', won 400 m gold at the 1924 Paris Olympics?
questions.x: Liddell refused to run the 100 m because the heats were on a Sunday. He later became a missionary in China.

questions.q: Which Dutch athlete won four gold medals at the 1948 London Olympics?
questions.x: The mother of two won the 100 m, 200 m, 80 m hurdles and 4x100 m relay, earning the nickname 'the Flying Housewife'.

questions.q: Which city hosted the 1948 'Austerity Games', the first Olympics after World War II?
questions.x: Rationing was still in force, so athletes were housed in military camps and colleges rather than a purpose-built village.

questions.q: Which country won the Olympic field hockey gold at six consecutive Games from 1928 to 1956?
questions.x: India won with a total goal difference of 178 to 7 across the six tournaments. Dhyan Chand was its star.

questions.q: Which Asian nation reached the World Cup semi-finals in 2002 as co-host?
questions.x: The Koreans beat Italy and Spain on the way, before losing to Germany in the semi-finals and finishing fourth.

questions.q: Which African nation became the first to reach a World Cup quarter-final, in 1990?
questions.x: Cameroon, led by veteran Roger Milla, lost to England 3-2 after extra time in the quarter-final. Milla celebrated his goals with a corner-flag dance.

questions.q: Which club won the first five European Cups, from 1956 to 1960?
questions.x: Real Madrid, led by Alfredo Di Stefano and Ferenc Puskas, beat Eintracht Frankfurt 7-3 in the 1960 final at Hampden Park.

questions.q: Which Scottish club became the first British team to win the European Cup, in 1967?
questions.x: Celtic beat Inter Milan 2-1 in Lisbon, with a team all born within about 30 miles of Glasgow. They became known as the 'Lisbon Lions'.

questions.q: What is the oldest national football competition in the world, founded in 1871?
questions.x: The first final in 1872 was won by Wanderers, who beat the Royal Engineers 1-0 at the Kennington Oval.

questions.q: Antonin Panenka chipped a famous penalty to win the Euro 1976 final for which country?
questions.x: The penalty beat West Germany's goalkeeper Sepp Maier in the first-ever European Championship final to be decided by a shootout.

questions.q: Which Italian defensive system, meaning 'door-bolt', became famous in the 1960s?
questions.x: Inter Milan coach Helenio Herrera used it to win two European Cups. It focused on a strong, organized defense and quick counter-attacks.

questions.q: Which ancient Chinese ball game is recognized by FIFA as an early form of football?
questions.x: Cuju, which means 'kick ball', was played during the Han dynasty more than 2,000 years ago, with players aiming a ball into a net.

questions.q: Which English club, founded in 1857, is recognized as the world's oldest football club?
questions.x: Sheffield FC wrote the Sheffield Rules, which influenced the modern game, including the introduction of corner kicks and heading the ball.

questions.q: Which team beat the 'Magical Magyars' of Hungary in the 1954 World Cup final?
questions.x: Hungary had been unbeaten for four years. West Germany came back from 2-0 down to win 3-2 in what is called the 'Miracle of Bern'.

questions.q: In cricket, a googly is a deceptive delivery bowled by which type of bowler?
questions.x: It looks like a normal leg break but turns the other way. It was invented by English bowler Bernard Bosanquet around 1900, so it is also called a 'bosie'.

questions.q: Which bearded Victorian is regarded as cricket's first superstar?
questions.x: Grace played first-class cricket for 44 years and was also a doctor. His beard made him one of the most recognizable Britons of his time.

questions.q: How many hurdles must athletes clear in the 400 m hurdles?
questions.x: The hurdles are spaced 35 meters apart. Each is 91.4 cm high for men and 76.2 cm for women.

questions.q: Which American won four gold medals at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, matching Jesse Owens's feat?
questions.x: Lewis won the 100 m, 200 m, long jump and 4x100 m relay, the same four events as Owens in 1936.

questions.q: Which Finnish runner won both the 5,000 m and 10,000 m at the 1972 and 1976 Olympics?
questions.x: Viren fell in the 10,000 m in 1972 but still got up to win with a world record. He repeated the double four years later.

questions.q: How many teams took part in the first World Cup in 1930?
questions.x: Only four European teams made the long sea voyage to Uruguay: Belgium, France, Romania and Yugoslavia.

questions.q: The Cresta Run, near St. Moritz, is a famous course for which sport?
questions.x: Riders slide headfirst on a small sled down a natural ice channel. The run was first built in the 1880s by British visitors.

questions.q: In which Canadian city was the first recorded indoor ice hockey game played in 1875?
questions.x: The game took place at the Victoria Skating Rink. It used a wooden puck rather than a ball to prevent it from hitting spectators.

questions.q: Which American became the first Black man to win the Wimbledon singles title, in 1975?
questions.x: Ashe stunned the heavily favored Jimmy Connors in the final. He had also won the US Open in 1968.

questions.q: In which country did 17-year-old Pele win his first World Cup in 1958?
questions.x: Pele scored twice in the final as Brazil beat the hosts Sweden 5-2. He became the youngest scorer in a World Cup final.

questions.q: Which method, named after two statisticians, is used to set targets in rain-affected limited-overs cricket?
questions.x: Tony Lewis and Frank Duckworth devised the system, first used in international cricket in 1997.

questions.q: Which Scottish sprinter won the 100 m at the 1980 Moscow Olympics?
questions.x: Wells won the 100 m by a hair over Cuba's Silvio Leonard. He later said he was inspired by his wife, who coached him.
